newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - BA cut to "sell" at SocGen.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - BA cut to "sell" at SocGen.

text.p: British Airways Plc was cut to a "sell" from a "hold" at SocGen, analyst Andy Chambers at the brokerage said on Thursday. SocGen also cut its profit forecasts for the company.

Chambers said the action reflected unfavourable currency rates, high fuel prices and a shift in the mix of passengers. He said there was also concern about possible setbacks to the proposed alliance between BA and American Airlines
"There are a lot of hurdles to be cleared before the deal can be signed," said Chambers. "And there has been some erosion of potential benefits from the link-up."
BA on Wednesday put its 25 percent stake in USAir Group up for sale, and may lose some Heathrow slots if Britain and the U.S. agree an "open skies" pact linked to the signing of the BA-American deal.

"With USAir no longer in the equation, BA will lose business on North Atlantic routes," Chambers said. Chambers said he saw some reduction of BA's passenger yield next year. "We're being fairly cautious," he said, adding that his price-earnings ratio forecast for March 1988 was at a 10 percent discount to the rest of the market.
The stock was up 6-1/2p at 607-1/2 by 1309 GMT.
